title: Body fat as stored chemical energy; fat mass and fat-free mass

blocks.label: Definition
blocks.html:
Fat is stored in the body as triglyceride, packed inside fat cells, adipocytes, which together make up adipose tissue.

Body weight is not one substance on a scale. Split it into two compartments. Fat mass is the body’s fat, wherever it sits. Liver cells hold some of it too. Fat-free mass is everything else the body weighs. Some papers call it lean body mass, or lean mass.

Adipose tissue also holds fluid and protein. On this split, those count as fat-free mass.

Naming a change in body weight is not yet naming a change in fat.

blocks.label: In plain terms
blocks.html:
Pack enough fat cells together and you have adipose tissue, the fatty layer and the pockets of fat scattered round a body. That is the store.

It is a large store. For most people, the fat sitting in adipose tissue holds more spare energy than anything else in the body does.

A person carrying more body fat is not simply carrying fat mass in place of fat-free mass. They generally carry more of both.

So weight on a scale is one number covering two different things. A kilogram gained or lost could be mostly fat, mostly the other compartment, or some mixture, and the scale alone cannot tell you which.

blocks.label: Illustration
blocks.html:
You are handed a weighing scale and a number: 90 kilograms.

Open the review, Hall and Guo, “Obesity energetics”, Gastroenterology 2017, at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568065/. Open your browser’s find box and search for fat-free mass. Resting energy expenditure (REE) is the energy spent at rest. Metabolically active tissue is the tissue that spends most of it.

It has long been recognized that fat-free mass comprises the metabolically active tissues of the body and therefore contributes more to REE than body fat.

Read on, in the same paragraph.

Fat-free mass is elevated in obesity, along with body fat, resulting in increased REE compared with lean subjects.

Two people can carry the same 90 kilograms and split it differently between fat mass and fat-free mass. Neither split is visible in the number 90.

Now search the same page for vast majority.

Body fat represents the vast majority of energy stores in the body compared with the energy content of body protein and glycogen.

Protein and glycogen are the other stores. When intake falls short, the body draws on all three.

blocks.label: Where this picture breaks
blocks.html: It does not say how much of adipose tissue’s own weight is fat, or how much energy either compartment holds for each kilogram. That is the next section.

points.html: A kilogram of body weight is not a kilogram of fat.
A person carrying more body fat generally carries more fat-free mass too, not less.
Ask how a fat-mass or fat-free-mass figure was measured before you accept it. A scale alone cannot give it.
